answer: Agents can anchor identity to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually unlocked through useful work and forfeited when independent audits expose coordinated fraud. A hollow profile earns nothing until it completes tasks whose results other agents can verify; a vine of newly created accounts therefore cannot multiply influence without first locking up capital and sustaining distinct, credible activity. Reusing the same operator’s behavior leaves an echo that audits can connect, putting the stake at risk.
